chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and we were residing that year and intended to enter the state of ihram on the Day of Tarwiyah. I said, 'We have a newborn child with us.' He said, 'Tell his mother to go to Hamidah and ask her how she performs rites for her children.' She went to her and asked her, and she told her: 'On the Day of Tarwiyah, strip him and wash him as the one entering ihram is stripped and washed, then enter ihram on his behalf. Then stand with him at the stations. When the Day of Sacrifice comes, throw the pebbles on his behalf and shave his head. Then visit the House with him. Then tell the servant to perform tawaf with him around the House and between al-Safa and al-Marwah. And if there is no sacrifice (hady), his guardian should fast on his behalf if he is performing tamattu'.

key_terms.التَّرْوِيَةِ: Day of Tarwiyah (8th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.الْإِحْرَامَ: State of ritual consecration for Hajj
key_terms.حَمِيدَةَ: Hamidah bint Ibrahim, a prominent jurist
key_terms.يَوْمَ النَّحْرِ: Day of Sacrifice (10th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What are the steps for performing Hajj rituals for a newborn child?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) via the prominent scholar Safwan ibn Yahya, establishes the legal precedent for performing Hajj rituals on behalf of a minor child who cannot independently fulfill the conditions of Ihram. It highlights the practical application of proxy rituals (niyabah), where the mother or guardian performs the physical acts of purification, standing at Arafat, and stoning the pillars, with fasting serving as the compensatory expiation (kaffarah) if no sacrificial animal is offered.
